$comment: Relative imports carry an explicit `.ts` extension because `node --test` runs the sources
directly with type stripping, and Node does not map `./x.js` onto `./x.ts` (verified:
`rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` (TypeScript >= 5.7) rewrites it to `.js` on emit, so the
built `lib/` graph is still resolvable by Node. Verified on tsc 5.9.3.
`src/client` is excluded here and built by tsconfig.client.json: that half is a browser
script (DOM lib, CommonJS, no node types) that must land at exactly `lib/client.js`, and one
config cannot be both halves. Two configs, two output graphs, no shared file.
